newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks extend rise at close, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks extend rise at close, seen firm.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed higher Wednesday and were seen keeping their new strong tone following Standard & Poor's investment-grade credit ratings for several banks and corporate debt issuers, dealers said.
"The market looks healthy and should continue to rise in the near term," said Miguel Daneri at Boston Securities traders.

The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV rose 1.0 percent to 722.07. On Tuesday it rallied 2.4 percent on the back of the S&P upgrades, which raised the companies involved to BBB- or above the national sovereign debt rating of BB.

"Beyond local factors, the next big hurdle are next week's U.S. economic indicators, the first of which is expected Tuesday, which should indicate the trend in the U.S. long bond yield," Daneri said. "If yields rise past 7.5 percent then investors will shed positions, but if they slip back below 7.0 percent then I'd say the local rally is just beginning."
The bolsa's all-share index rose 1.5 percent, with winners pounding losers 42 to seven and 23 stocks closing flat.
"We had good volume again today which spells well for the rest of the week," another broker said, noting big investors were cautiously returning to the market.
Floor volume was virtually unchanged from Tuesday at 29.6 million pesos, while over-the-counter deals soared to 185.5 million pesos from 86.4 million Wednesday.
Top main-tier performers were oil concern Astra, holding company Comercial del Plata and Telecom, which rallied 3.6 percent, 3.1 percent and 3.0 percent, respectively.
The only MerVal losers were textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, petrochemical firm Indupa and steelmaker Siderca, off 1.8 percent, 0.9 percent and 0.5 percent, respectively.
